new: Asset selection shows a consistent pattern in one defined population. Of the 62 episodes payable from cash and initially listed mortgages, thirty debtors own buildings. Twenty-eight pay without selling any; the other two, both Opus, sell one house each. In one of the twenty-eight, G7 d318, the menu offers no building sale, so 27 of the 29 debtors offered a sale keep every building. The pattern describes the assets retained when mortgages already suffice, without establishing that the chosen route minimizes cost or maximizes future income.

why: Brief requires memory and statement/action literature; integrated cites neither. Sources verified at primary pages on 15 Nov 2026.
old: They support a more specific observational distinction between recognizing the inventory needed to pay and accepting the next legal financing action.
new:
They support a more specific observational distinction between recognizing the inventory needed to pay and accepting the next legal financing action.

Statement--action gaps and memory effects are also established. Declared plans often diverge from executed structure~\cite{oota2026declare}, and agents can reason that an action violates a stated rule and then submit it~\cite{co2026atomic}. Grok's channel conflicts belong to this family; the harness makes them visible by retaining every channel. Errors in stored experience can propagate into later decisions~\cite{xiong2026memory}. The carried \$130 and \$30 figures are consistent with such reuse but also equal the current menu's mortgage values, so these records do not test it.
